newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Belgian PM says 3 pct deficit goal key for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM says 3 pct deficit goal key for EMU.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Thursday entrants into Europe's single currency would have to keep their budget deficits as close as possible to the three percent criteria.
"The objective is to be as near as possible to three percent and to be under three percent if possible," he told Reuters Financial Television.
Dehaene also said delaying Europe's monetary union (EMU) beyond its planned starting date in January 1999 to give countries more time to get their deficits under control was not an option.
"I think it is the worst option and it's an impossible option," he said. "We have no other choice than to start on time."
Dehaene added that a delay in EMU would hit Germany worst.

"I am convinced that the need to start on time is perhaps the biggest for Germany," he said in English. "If EMU does not start on time all finanical markets will run to the mark and that will be a big problem for Germany." -- Knut Engelmann, Salzburg newsroom +43-662 870 367
